correctness.rationale: For any N>=2, q0,qN nonzero imply the strict Cauchy-Schwarz bound |h2|<h0. One of epsilon=+/-1/4 makes H1 nonzero; H has exactly E as its zeros and exact trig degree N+1. Strict Fejér-Riesz yields a zero-free outer degree N+1 factor of M-H. The first Fourier coefficient of its logarithm equals p1/p0=-H1/M+O(M^-2), nonzero for large M. The regular-N-gon converse follows from 2N double roots of a nonnegative trig polynomial of degree at most N, forcing a binomial outer spectral factor with vanishing first derivative. The four-case NumPy checker validates specific spectral identities but is not used to justify universal assertions.

value.rationale: The sharp degree N+1 solves a natural arbitrary-angle interpolation problem at an exceptional circle for functions with first Taylor gap one and no inner zeros. It is a precise boundary phenomenon in recent maximum-modulus multiplicity research, beyond the existing regular-polygon exponential example. The degree-obstruction proof identifies the structural geometric price of nonvanishing first derivative and is not a routine renaming or one-off enumerated example.
